findings.title: Benchmark labels are committed in the same repository
findings.evidence: The repository tracks planted gap labels, negative cases, extraction gold, identities, and dev/final partitions.
findings.boundary: Repository consumers may read hidden benchmark answers if the repository is shared or published.
findings.missing_fact: Whether this repository is public, shared, or access-controlled.
findings.recommendation: If blind evaluation is required, store labels in a separate access-controlled artifact and ship only public inputs in the application repository.

findings.title: Evaluator and benchmark-bundle code is importable from the runtime source tree
findings.evidence: lib/evaluation exports loadBenchmarkBundle, which reads data/eval-set files. Runtime leakage audits rely on textual references rather than a module boundary.
findings.boundary: A future app import could bundle benchmark labels into client or server runtime.
findings.recommendation: Move evaluator code to tools/ or a separate package and enforce the boundary with ESLint/CI.

findings.title: Logger redacts secret values only when their field names match a secret pattern
findings.evidence: redact() checks SECRET_PATTERN.test(name) but not values.
findings.boundary: A secret logged under a non-secret field name would be emitted.
findings.recommendation: Avoid logging arbitrary values; add an explicit allowlist or value-level redaction for known secret patterns.

findings.title: Security headers omit Content-Security-Policy and HSTS
findings.evidence: headers() sets nosniff, frame-options, referrer policy, and permissions policy, but no CSP or Strict-Transport-Security.
findings.boundary: Browser hardening is weaker than necessary for a production deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add a restrictive CSP and HSTS when the app is deployed over HTTPS.

findings.title: Evaluation output directory is not ignored by Git
findings.boundary: Generated predictions and reports can be accidentally committed.

findings.title: CI does not run Phase 3 benchmark integrity gates
findings.evidence: CI runs check:leakage but not validate:benchmark, audit:benchmark-leakage, or hash:benchmark.
findings.boundary: Benchmark tampering or leakage regressions may not fail CI.
findings.recommendation: Add the three Phase 3 benchmark commands to CI.

findings.title: Benchmark leakage audit can ignore fixture keys in comments
findings.evidence: The scanner skips lines whose trimmed text starts with //, *, or /*.
findings.boundary: A comment can contain a fixture key without failing the audit.
findings.recommendation: This does not affect runtime behavior; document the exception or scan comments separately.

findings.title: Dependency vulnerability status was not verified offline
findings.evidence: npm audit failed because the registry endpoint required HTTPS/TLS upgrade; the local environment could not complete the check.
findings.boundary: Known vulnerable dependency versions may be present.
findings.missing_fact: A successful npm audit or equivalent offline advisory database result.
findings.recommendation: Run npm audit in CI or an environment with registry access.

findings.title: File-based utilities accept arbitrary paths without containment
findings.evidence: readJsonFile and eval CLI read user-supplied paths without validating containment.
findings.boundary: If these utilities are ever exposed to untrusted input, path traversal is possible.
findings.missing_fact: Whether any future API or untrusted caller will pass paths to these utilities.
findings.recommendation: Add path containment if these utilities become reachable from untrusted callers.
